title: The Body and its Members
english: …suppers of their own they hurried. These they laid on lavishly in the church, as if to show up the want of those who had nothing, since they got drunk while others went hungry. They got in ahead of the communion and enjoyed their own fine food.

On 1 Corinthians 12:1–2: By “spiritual gifts” he now means the workings of the Holy Spirit, which he distributes to each according to worth: to one to preach the gospel, to another to prophesy, to another something else. By saying “you were led away to the idols,” he shows how very different prophecy is from soothsaying. At the idols, those possessed by the unclean spirit are not sober. They are carried off by the unclean spirit and do not go by their own free choice; that is what he shows by “you were led away,” carried off as they were. So he says: you know from what you went through how the unclean spirit works, but the gifts of the Holy Spirit work purely. So the soothsayer is darkened in soul and does not know what he is saying, while the prophet's soul grows brighter; it learns what it did not know and speaks what has been revealed to it. The demon, as an enemy, darkens the soul; the Spirit, as a benefactor, comes to the soul and gives it light. He goes on to show this.

On 1 Corinthians 12:3: Everything blasphemous against Christ is worked by the evil one, who clouds the soul. He says this to guard them against those who pretend to be carried by God and yet speak against Christ. Legion and the Pythian soothsayer both named the Lord Jesus, so we do not say that whoever says this says it perfectly, since many righteous men are called “lords.” What counts is to confess Christ's lordship and mastery over all. Perhaps, too, they said it to test him, as the devil did when he took him up onto the mountain (Matthew 4:8). That is why he does not accept their witness either, since it came from the unworthy and from those testing him.

On 1 Corinthians 12:8–10: “The word of wisdom” is to understand what was spoken in God's wisdom in the prophets and evangelists, and to set it before the hearers. “The word of knowledge” is the revelation of hidden things, which someone who did not know them at first learns from grace and then speaks. “Faith” is simply believing the preaching: merely hearing it is not faith; faith is receiving faithfully what has been said. “Discernment of spirits”: soothsaying has copied prophecy, in that in soothsaying too the Holy Spirit seems to foretell, so he has given the power to tell these apart, so that we are not led astray.

On 1 Corinthians 12:12: He pictures Christ by the whole body made up of many members, meaning the church by “Christ.” Christ is called the head of the church and the church the body of Christ, and here he has named the church “Christ,” pointing to the lesser by the greater.
On 1 Corinthians 12:14: He says this so that they do not look down on the humbler members of the church. Even if someone is lesser by nature, he still contributes to the common good of the church.
On 1 Corinthians 12:27: He did not say “members from members” but “many members from one member,” for the head of the whole body is a member.

On 1 Corinthians 12:28: Since he has spoken of members and a body, he starts from the most honored of the other members after the head, the apostles. By “prophets” he means those in the church, not those under the law. Third, teachers. Do not be surprised that the teacher is placed ahead of those who work healings and mighty deeds. The signs are there so that the knowledge may be believed, and the knowledge is set before people by those who teach. “Helps”: he speaks of this elsewhere: “he who leads, with diligence” (Romans 12:8). “Administrations”: the governing of the church.

On 1 Corinthians 12:31: For this reason he shows that they took great pride in the gift of tongues, and in the other gifts too. So he shows that love is the greatest thing. Those other gifts are given even…

translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix-b2): the old English was garbled ("for envying the fellowship, they deprived others of their own sight", "the evil one who thunders at the soul"), printed labels as "Concerning 1 Cor 12:1-2" and "Regarding 1 Cor 12:3", and filed the 12:28 note under the 12:27 label. Retranslated every clause from the Greek. Labels: the edition's 1 Kor 12,27 covers two notes; the first ("members from one member") is on 12:27, the second ("Since he has spoken of members ... apostles, prophets, teachers, helps, administrations") is on 12:28 and is now labeled 12:28. Doublet collapsed: the second form at 264,col2 on 12:27-28 ("Christ is head of the church; after that member he calls the apostles second members; not those under the law but those of the church") repeats the first and is not printed. The rest of that column, on 12:31, has no counterpart earlier and is kept in full; the edition prints no verse label for it, so the label 12:31 is taken from the lemma it quotes (ποθεῖτε τὰ χαρίσματα τὰ κρείττονα, in u05-rem-early). Section begins and ends mid-sentence.
